title: Act, observe, decide
intro: An agent loop alternates an action, an observation and a decision about what to do next. The controller enforces continuation and stopping rules.
takeaway: A loop requires evidence and boundaries; repeated prompting alone does not enforce them.

beats.text: The agent proposes an action. The tool executes the permitted operation.
The tool returns an observation. The controller receives actual evidence.
The controller checks the stopping rules. It decides whether another step is allowed.
If allowed, another action can follow. The cycle has an explicit decision point.

title: Use a specific failure
intro: A discount-calculation test fails with a concrete assertion. The agent can connect that observation to a targeted code change.
takeaway: A failing assertion is useful only when the relevant tests actually ran. Preserve the failing input and expected behavior.

beats.text: Twelve tests run against the code. One assertion fails.
Send the failing assertion to the agent. It shows expected and actual behavior.
The agent makes a targeted repair. The code changes; the evidence is now old.
Return the changed code to the runner. The next observation must be fresh.

title: Stop after verified success
intro: The repaired code runs through the selected suite again. When the configured success criteria are met, the edit loop stops and hands over evidence.
takeaway: Passing this suite supports the tested behavior. It does not establish that all possible behavior is correct.

beats.text: Run the same relevant checks again. This time, test the repaired revision.
All twelve selected tests pass. The runner reports what actually ran.
The controller checks the success rule. The observed result satisfies this rule.
Stop editing and hand over the evidence. Unrequested edits add uncertainty.

title: No tests is not a pass
intro: A mistyped test selector can select zero tests. Under this repair-only policy, the agent stops rather than treating the empty run as proof of correctness.
takeaway: Distinguish assertion failure, collection errors and no tests selected. They require different next actions.

beats.text: A selector matches no tests. No behavior has been checked.
The runner returns that empty selection. The agent cannot call it a passing suite.
This policy stops further code edits. Keep the command and selection output.
Hand the evidence to an engineer. Repair the test setup before continuing.

title: Limit repair attempts
intro: A controller can cap time, tool calls or repair attempts. Repeated unproductive failures should lead to a useful handoff rather than an endless loop.
takeaway: The controller must enforce the budget outside the model. A handoff should explain what was tried and what still fails.

beats.text: The task has a configured attempt budget. The controller counts completed attempts.
Another repair attempt still fails. The remaining allowance decreases.
The budget is exhausted. The controller blocks another edit cycle.
Send the remaining failure and evidence. A human can choose a new approach.
